detail: Quote joins two claims; the second (new curricula teach IT skills) is digital skills not linked to a technology recommendation (R2). Recut to 'The digitalisation of the economy is advancing' and summary rewritten.

Recommendation on recruiting IT staff for the public administration: staffing is the subject rather than the technology, so the materiality test is uncertain; theme_doubtful flag arguably needed (compare MKD-IO-2024-001-0053, which is flagged). Rules do not say whether IT staffing of digital services meets the test.

'No progress was noted on coordination, communication and responsiveness to PDPA recommendations' uses the standard progress wording for a sub-area; eu_scale.progress_level should be 'No progress', applies_to sub_area (as for -0063).

Quote starts with a separate finding ('There was some progress in ICT infrastructure development', a standard-scale sub-area statement). Recut the metric quote to start at 'fixed broadband was available'; the finding is added as a missed item (-0205).

Status in_practice is not supported by the wording ('does not distinguish' describes the law's content, says nothing about application); 'adopted' or 'unclear' would fit better. Rules give no status for a law described as in force.
Status in_practice for a plan that 'remains valid': the wording says the plan is in force, not that it is applied. Rules give no status for 'remains valid' (adopted or unclear would be closer).
'has taken steps towards' the digital transformation of education, with EMIS still being piloted: the source describes work under way, so stated_status should be in_progress (R5), not implemented.

'Good progress was noted in the consolidation and upgrading of IT systems' is standard progress wording for a sub-area; record progress_level 'Good progress', applies_to sub_area (R3), not leave eu_scale empty.
